citations.assessment: The homily identifies Menaḥem explicitly as the son-in-law of Elazar, using bar Rabbi Avina in this witness.
This homily states both the kinship, with Avunah, and the transmission in the name of Shimon son of Yosna.
The companion homily confirms the same kinship, with Avuna, and names Yaakov bar Avina as the authority for the teaching.

holds.raw: ומ' מגילה פסוק והשתיה כדת בש"ר יעקב בר אבונא
holds.reason: Esther Rabbah comments on the verse without the named attribution in the compared text. Song of Songs Rabbah gives Yaakov bar Avina for a distinct teaching. The exact Esther midrash occurrence remains unlocated.
